u(t)=U(t)u_0-\int_0^t U(t-\tau)(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x(u^p)\,d\tau,
\]
where \(U(t)\) is unitary on \(H^s\) and \((1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x\) is bounded \(H^{s-1}\to H^s\). Hence the \(p\)-th Picard iterate defines a bounded map \(H^s\to C([0,T];H^s)\) iff the \(p\)-linear product map
\[
(f_1,\dots,f_p)\mapsto f_1\cdots f_p
\]
is bounded \(H^s\times\cdots\times H^s\to H^{s-1}\).

Take \(u_0\) with \(\widehat u_0\) a plateau of height \(A\) and width \(N\) supported on \(\pm[N,2N]\). Then \(\|u_0\|_{H^s}\sim A N^{s+1/2}\). The balanced \(p\)-fold convolution (half the factors from \(+N\), half from \(-N\)) produces a low-frequency plateau of height \(\sim A^p N^{p-1}\) on \(|\xi|\lesssim N\). For \(s<1/2\),
\[
\|u_0^p\|_{H^{s-1}}\sim A^p N^{p-1}\Big(\int_{|\xi|<N}(1+\xi^2)^{s-1}d\xi\Big)^{1/2}\sim A^p N^{p-1}.
\]
Boundedness therefore requires \(N^{p-1}\lesssim N^{p(s+1/2)}\), i.e.
\[
p-1\le ps+\frac p2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\ge \frac12-\frac1p.
\]
All other frequency interactions give weaker constraints. Conversely, for \(s\ge \frac12-\frac1p\) this \(p\)-linear estimate holds, giving unconditional local well-posedness in \(C([0,T];H^s)\); for \(s<\frac12-\frac1p\) the \(p\)-th iterate blows up as \(N\to\infty\), so the flow map cannot be \(C^p\) at the origin.

**Derivation.**  
Write the Duhamel form
\[
u(t)=S(t)u_0-\int_0^t S(t-\tau)\,(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x\bigl(u(\tau)^p\bigr)\,d\tau,\qquad S(t)=e^{-t(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x}.
\]
The $C^p$-differentiability of the flow map at the origin is controlled by the $p$-linear term
\[
M_p(\varphi)=\int_0^t S(t-\tau)\,(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x\bigl[(S(\tau)\varphi)^p\bigr]\,d\tau .
\]

Test it on a highly concentrated, norm-one packet. On $\mathbb R$ take $\varphi_N(x)=N^{1/2-s}\psi(Nx)e^{iNx}$ with a fixed bump $\psi$; on $\mathbb T$ take $\varphi_N\sim N^{-s-1/2}\sum_{N< n\le 2N}e^{inx}$. In both cases $\|\varphi_N\|_{H^s}\approx1$ and the packet has spatial width $\sim N^{-1}$.

Because $S(\tau)$ is unitary on $H^s$ and, at frequency $\sim N$, $(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x\partial_x\approx -\mathrm{Id}$, one has
\[
\|M_p(\varphi_N)\|_{H^s}\sim t\,\|\varphi_N^p\|_{H^s}
\sim t\,N^{(p-1)(1/2-s)} .
\]
Hence $\|M_p(\varphi_N)\|_{H^s}\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$ whenever $s<1/2$, so the flow map cannot be $C^p$ there. For $s>1/2$ the exponent is negative and the $p$-linear estimate holds.

Conversely, for $s>1/2$ (on both $\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb T$) $H^s$ is an algebra, so $u\mapsto(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x(u^p)$ is locally Lipschitz $H^s\to H^s$; Picard iteration gives unconditional local well-posedness in $C([0,T];H^s)$.

Thus the sharp threshold is $s_c(p)=1/2$, independent of $p$.
